title: Skyveil Horizon: Update to game, almost ready for online testing
author: Mindless_Software_99
selftext:
I made a lot of updates to the game Project Anime Glider. Calling it Skyveil Horizon. It is going to be an online multiplayer game that takes elements of Kirby Air Ride's City Trial, RPG elements, and MOBA elements.

I will be looking for testers soon so if you are interested in testing out the game, please let me know in the comments.

If you have any character recommendations, definitely let me know and I may add them to the game! Feedback is also appreciated.

comments.author: maddix_cummings
comments.body:
I'll be honest, it's jarring. It's very easy to tell you let the AI do what it does well and didn't preoccupy much with what it can't do well or where you have gaps in knowledge. Your UI is gorgeous, slick and modern, while your environment looks like a Crash Bandicoot HD Remake. I'm exaggerating of course, but with AI it feels like seeing a revival of these asset flip games where one asset was high quality while the rest varied greatly.

What I mean to say is that it's really cohesive so far and your description is pretty vague. It's "elements" (not defining which elements) of Kirby Air Ride's City Trial, RPG elements (what does it even mean in your case?) and MOBA elements. Nothing tells a player how these systems play off each other or if there's even systems to begin with. "Testers" is vague too  so far the only thing one could give feedback to is your hoverboard feel, which, it's good to get feedback, but feels a little early considering people won't even know what the goal of handling this hoverboard is. It's just a bit underbaked. You have aiming and an animation for it, but no look at feature that shows your character following the reticle. You're gonna get basic feedback like this which is a bit useless considering you probably know it and your feedback should focus on gamefeel, not basic UX that you probably already know.

Also, just personal advice: if your game is multiplayer and especially a MOBA or online RPG, start with network. Your video doesn't show any network capacity. The first thing you  should look at is the multiplayer side, not whether the solo hoverboard works.

replies.author: SirStarshine
replies.body: You make a good point about details and clarification on mechanics and their purposes. Maybe OP could share part of their game doc. Personally, I really like what I see so far. The only complaint I have is that the triggers don't seem to go off properly on the hoverboard. I hear too many interaction sounds when they're riding and nothing is happening.

replies.author: maddix_cummings
replies.body: Nothing wrong with liking what *you* see, but then I wouldn't recommend seeking feedback from opposing views. Or distributing a game for other people. That's kinda the whole point of feedback.

replies.author: amirati91
replies.body:
Yes, the young man is right on every point.

I would add a single point, if you want the game to be distributed commercially, or have some commercial pretense, it seems to me a lot of work away until I reach the first players for testing.

It has a prototype face, assets with volatile qualities, generic in some way which is not demerit in any project. It all starts like this. I think it's just a matter of understanding the time to show the world. Talking to others who also make games is a way to get feedback, but not the whole, because the whole is in a very early stage, and Reddit is so polluted with one shots and cheap copies of other games that people, as you may have noticed in other comments, are not kind to the observations.
Anyway, it's an interesting principle. But still some time away until it has its own face.

Just my 2 cents.

comments.author: perpetual_stew
comments.body:
There's one thing I'm wondering about a lot of AI games like this.  I see a lot of games that tend to be an animated 3d character navigating a flat 3d world which looks ok.  I don't have a lot of game development experience with this type of game, but I would have thought this was a solved problem that doesn't need programming?  Like, you can easily animate a character with Mixamo, for example, so I would have thought this was literally something where you drop in assets and draw a map and everything is taken care of for you by the engine?   Maybe I'm wrong, but even so it seems like a animated character + world game generator would be a pretty trivial thing to make even before LLM coding. 

Don't get me wrong, I think it's nice that you are setting up a full playable game with the whole character setup process and stuff.  But it seems like the game itself is just generic assets on a 2d field?

replies.author: FarAd7559
replies.body:
Well yes-no.

If you can really translate a significant portion of the itch and unity games rollout back before 2020s that these games really just drop assets-and-pray for most of the time.

But tbf, yes I think most of the main reason is to create at least the incentive of exploration. There's a reason why there's constraints on some thing in gaming, and if you really push it to hard on just put your character into a wide field while leaving them nothing to do is exactly what it is you're talking about. That's why game mechanics and lore exists, and the main problem in this demo is that even in lore perspective it needs polishing on for "why" the characters need to progress in the first place.

Even in games like GTA or many open sandbox environment, you have to sugarcoat the player to make them do something. If you just expect them to walk around endlessly while really getting on smaller and lighter aspects, then you would expect them to get bored quickly.

comments.author: Antiox123456
comments.body: Honestly, it screams AI-slop. It feels like you're just trying to make a cheap copy of Genshin Impact rather than creating something original.

replies.author: darkoblivion000
replies.body:
That was exactly what came to mind for me.

Feels like an empty world no story version of Genshin impact. Which is free to play.
